signals.title: @mrldgg: Eight months after the Pentagon established Project Maven, its first computer vision capability was operating in combat. Katrina Manson's Pr
signals.content: Eight months after the Pentagon established Project Maven, its first computer vision capability was operating in combat. Katrina Manson's Project Maven follows Marine Colonel Drew Cukor and the small team that made that happen, building AI capability inside a bureaucracy designed to acquire tanks and ships, not software. Her account focuses less on algorithms than on institutional resistance, wartime urgency, and why this effort succeeded where so many defense innovation programs stall. Manson earned the trust of the notoriously private Cukor, and her reporting shows. Phil Gentile's review at The Military Reading Room places the book in the larger transition toward AI-enabled decision-making across the Joint Force. Link in bio.
